place.en: The hidden realm · Below the drop

setup.zh: 爬到一半，底下有了火光。崖下一道窄窄的石台，一面光秃秃的石墙——墙后头，有风。墙脚一汪半干的水潭，潭边卧着一块碾盘大的黑石头：白身赤首、像龟的蛫。内门那个九层劈了它一剑，叫它拖进了潭里。
setup.en: Halfway down there is firelight below. Under the cliff, a narrow stone ledge and a bare stone wall — and behind the wall, wind. At its foot a half-dry pool, and by the pool lies a black stone the size of a millstone: the gui, white body, red head, like a turtle. An inner-sect ninth layer struck it once with his sword and got dragged into the pool.

recap.zh: 凶崖底下，墙脚卧着一只蛫，渴得快死了。打不过的，不打：你把三天的水全倒进墙脚那个浅窝，檐上拿背绳吊了一块石头，底下绑着剑。它挪进窝里，墙里「轰隆隆」一响——它就是门闩；剑扎进它壳沿的裂纹，它咬穿了你的左小臂，你压着剑柄，一寸一寸。墙，开了。
recap.en: At the foot of the Cliff of Danger a gui lay by the wall, dying of thirst. What you can't beat, you don't fight: you poured all three days' water into the shallow hollow at the wall's foot, and from the overhang you hung a stone on your pack rope with the sword tied beneath it. It crawled into the hollow, and the wall gave a rumble — it was the latch; the sword went into the crack at the rim of its shell, it bit through your left forearm, and you bore down on the hilt, inch by inch. The wall opened.

zh: 凶崖底下。潭边，一只白身赤首的蛫。
en: "…This place. This queen has been here."
The foot of the Cliff of Danger. By the pool, a gui, white body, red head.

label.en: The shallow hollow at the wall's foot

text.zh: 墙脚的地上，凿着一个极大的浅窝，凿得溜光，窝底积着一层干泥：椭圆的，一头尖，四边各一个小凹——跟那口铁锅一般大小。
text.en: A huge shallow hollow cut in the ground, worn smooth, dry mud at the bottom: oval, pointed at one end, a little dip on each side — the size of that iron wok.

label.en: The water marks round the pool

text.zh: 潭边的石头上，一圈一圈，全是水印子，最高的一圈齐它的壳顶。如今那汪水，只剩一巴掌深。
text.en: The rocks round the pool are ringed with water marks, ring above ring, the highest level with the top of its shell. What water is left is a hand's depth.

text.zh: 你拔一根头发举到墙前。它往墙的方向飘了一飘，又一飘——倒像墙那边有一张嘴，隔着一层石头，在慢慢地吸气。
text.en: You pull out a hair and hold it to the wall. It drifts toward the wall, once, and again — as if behind it a mouth were slowly breathing in, through a layer of stone.

story.zh:
底下是一道窄窄的石台，站着两个内门的，提着剑的，便是河滩上拂袖子的那个九层。墙脚有一汪半干的水潭，潭边卧着一块碾盘大的黑石头。那「石头」前头探出一颗脑袋来，斗大，赤红赤红。九层回手一剑斩在它壳上，在壳沿靠脖子的地方崩出一道裂纹。那颗脑袋一伸，「喀」的一声，咬住了九层的肩膀和半边脖子，往潭里一拖。

这一头便是那面石墙，不见门，不见缝；墙脚的地上，凿着一个极大的浅窝，正上方的崖壁上，凸出一块石檐。银月道：「那面墙后头，有风透过来。」

那黑石头一动不动，壳像一口倒扣的大铁锅，铁黑铁黑；壳沿上一道一道的旧印子，刀砍的，铁器撬的，旧得发黑。

银月看了半天，道：「白身，赤首，像龟。……巴掌大的长成这样，怕是比本王还老。……[蛫]{注=gui}。有本书叫《山海经》{典=shanhai-gui}，写它『其狀如龜，而白身赤首』，『是可以禦火』。」

那汪水只剩一巴掌深。它渴得快死了。小满又看那个浅窝：跟那口铁锅一般大小。他想：这面墙，要的是它那一身分量。他打不过它。他爹说过：「打不过的，不打。给它下坠子。」
story.en:
Below was a narrow stone ledge with two inner-sect disciples on it; the one who held a sword was the ninth-layer who had swept his sleeve on the riverbed. At the foot of the wall was a half-dry pool, and beside the pool lay a black rock the size of a millstone. A head came out of the front of the "rock", big as a bushel, red as red. The ninth-layer swung back and struck its shell, cracking a line in the shell's rim near the neck. That head shot out, and with a *crack* it had the ninth-layer's shoulder and half his neck in its jaws and was dragging him into the pool.

At this end was the stone wall, no door, no crack. In the floor at the wall's foot a huge shallow hollow had been cut, and right above it a stone eave jutted from the cliff. Yinyue said: "Behind that wall, there's air coming through."

The black rock didn't move. Its shell was like a great iron pot turned upside down, black as iron; on the shell's rim were old marks, one after another, cut by blades, pried by iron tools, so old they'd gone black.

Yinyue watched a long time and said: "White body, red head, like a turtle... A palm-sized one grown to that, it's probably older than this queen... A [gui]{注=gui}. There's a book called the *Classic of Mountains and Seas*{典=shanhai-gui} that says of it, 'it is shaped like a turtle, with a white body and a red head,' and 'it can be used to ward off fire.'"

The water was only a hand deep. It was dying of thirst. Xiaoman looked at the shallow hollow again: the same size as that iron pot. He thought: what this wall wants is that whole weight of it. He couldn't beat it. His father used to say: "What you can't beat, you don't fight. You hang a deadfall on it."

story_full.zh:
爬到一半，底下有了火光。他把身子往崖上一道石缝里一塞，贴平了。底下是一道窄窄的石台，站着两个内门的，一个举着火折子；另一个提着剑，便是河滩上拂袖子的那个九层。九层绕着台上一面光秃秃的石墙敲了一圈，敲到墙脚，一剑劈了下去。

墙脚有一汪半干的水潭，潭边卧着一块碾盘大的黑石头——小满方才也只当它是一块石头。剑声一响，那「石头」前头探出一颗脑袋来，斗大，赤红赤红，像一颗烧透了的炭。九层回手一剑斩在它壳上，火星一迸，剑从壳上滑开，在壳沿靠脖子的地方崩出一道裂纹。它没有缩。那颗脑袋一伸，比剑还快，「喀」的一声，咬住了九层的肩膀和半边脖子，往潭里一拖。剑脱了手，当啷一声落在塌石边上。举火折子的那个，火折子一扔，扭头钻进塌石后头一道缝里——他们两个，原是从那里来的——一眼也没往回看。潭里扑腾了几下，便不扑腾了。

他没有下去。他贴在石缝里，把底下看了个遍。那道石台贴着崖根，只有三四步宽；往外再迈一步，又是黑的——那才是凶崖，深不见底，方才那一滴一滴的水声，便是从这底下上来的。石台外沿钉着一根锈烂了的铁橛子，橛子上拴着半截麻绳，垂在黑里。石台那一头，崖根底下堆着半人高一堆塌石；这一头便是那面石墙，一丈来高，不见门，不见缝；墙脚的地上，凿着一个极大的浅窝，凿得溜光，窝底积着一层干泥，正上方的崖壁上，凸出一块石檐。银月道：「那面墙后头，有风透过来。」

那黑石头一动不动，壳像一口倒扣的大铁锅，铁黑铁黑；壳沿上一道一道的旧印子，刀砍的，铁器撬的，旧得发黑。潭底除了方才那个九层，还躺着两副白骨，一副手里还攥着一把锈刀。

银月看了半天，道：「白身，赤首，像龟。……本王年轻的时候，在一座山上见过它们一窝，巴掌大，山里的人捡它们的壳挂在房梁底下，说是能挡火。巴掌大的长成这样，怕是比本王还老。……[蛫]{注=gui}。有本书叫《山海经》{典=shanhai-gui}，写它『其狀如龜，而白身赤首』，『是可以禦火』。」

崖上滚下来一粒小石子，落在它壳上，它不动。一只土鳖从塌石里爬出来，从它鼻子底下爬过去，它也不动；土鳖爬到潭边一沾水，那颗脑袋「喀」地出来了。隔一阵，它自己也往潭里探一探，探到底，又缩回去——那汪水只剩一巴掌深，潭边的石头上一圈一圈全是水印子，最高的一圈齐它的壳顶。它渴得快死了。壳沿那道新裂纹，往外渗着黑水。小满又看那个浅窝：椭圆的，一头尖，四边各一个小凹，跟那口铁锅一般大小。他想：这面墙，要的是它那一身分量。

他打不过它。河滩上那一拂袖子，他是看见了的；拂袖子的那一个，在它嘴底下，只够一口。他爹说过：「打不过的，不打。给它下坠子。」
story_full.en:
Halfway down there was firelight below. He wedged himself into a crack in the cliff and lay flat. Below was a narrow stone ledge with two inner-sect disciples on it, one holding a fire-stick; the other held a sword, and he was the ninth-layer who had swept his sleeve on the riverbed. The ninth-layer went all the way round a bare stone wall on the ledge, tapping it, and when he'd tapped down to its foot he brought his sword down hard.

At the foot of the wall was a half-dry pool, and beside the pool lay a black rock the size of a millstone. Xiaoman too had taken it for a rock. At the sound of the sword, a head came out of the front of the "rock", big as a bushel, red as red, like a coal burned through. The ninth-layer swung back and struck its shell; sparks flew, and the blade skidded off, cracking a line in the shell's rim near the neck. It didn't pull in. That head shot out, faster than the sword, and with a *crack* it had the ninth-layer's shoulder and half his neck in its jaws and was dragging him into the pool. The sword left his hand and fell with a clang by the fallen rocks. The one with the fire-stick threw it down, turned and dived into a crack behind the rockfall (that was where the two of them had come from) and didn't look back once. There was some thrashing in the pool, and then there wasn't.

He didn't go down. He lay in his crack and took in everything below. The ledge hugged the foot of the cliff and was only three or four paces wide; one step further out and it was black again. That was the real Deadly Cliff, bottomless, and the dripping he'd heard came up from down there. At the outer edge of the ledge an iron peg had been driven in, rusted almost through, with half a length of hemp rope tied to it, hanging down into the dark. At one end of the ledge, against the cliff foot, was a pile of fallen rock half a man high; at this end was the stone wall, a dozen feet high, no door, no crack. In the floor at the wall's foot a huge shallow hollow had been cut, worn smooth, with a layer of dried mud in the bottom, and right above it a stone eave jutted from the cliff. Yinyue said: "Behind that wall, there's air coming through."

The black rock didn't move. Its shell was like a great iron pot turned upside down, black as iron; on the shell's rim were old marks, one after another, cut by blades, pried by iron tools, so old they'd gone black. On the bottom of the pool, besides that ninth-layer just now, lay two sets of white bones, one still clutching a rusted knife.

Yinyue watched a long time and said: "White body, red head, like a turtle... When this queen was young, I saw a nest of them on a mountain, palm-sized, and the mountain folk picked up their shells and hung them under the roof beams. They said it kept fire away. A palm-sized one grown to that, it's probably older than this queen... A [gui]{注=gui}. There's a book called the *Classic of Mountains and Seas*{典=shanhai-gui} that says of it, 'it is shaped like a turtle, with a white body and a red head,' and 'it can be used to ward off fire.'"

A pebble rolled down from the cliff and landed on its shell; it didn't move. A woodlouse crawled out of the rockfall and crawled right past under its nose; it didn't move either. The woodlouse reached the edge of the pool and touched the water, and the head came out with a *crack*. Every so often it put its own head down into the pool, reached the bottom, and pulled back. The water was only a hand deep, and on the stones round the pool were water marks, ring above ring, the highest level with the top of its shell. It was dying of thirst. The new crack in the shell's rim was oozing black fluid. Xiaoman looked at the shallow hollow again: oval, pointed at one end, a small dip on each of its four sides, the same size as that iron pot. He thought: what this wall wants is that whole weight of it.

He couldn't beat it. He had seen that sleeve-sweep on the riverbed; the man who swept the sleeve had made one mouthful for it. His father used to say: "What you can't beat, you don't fight. You hang a deadfall on it."

exits.means: tries to pry the gui off the wall by force — the shell does not budge, it bites, the wall stays shut

snub.zh: 你拿竹筒去撬那口铁锅，撬了三回，纹丝不动；第四回，它一口咬在你手背上，血珠子冒了出来。壳沿上一道一道的旧印子，刀砍的，铁器撬的——前人也这么撬过。墙，没开。
snub.en: You lever at the iron pot with your flask, three times; it doesn't budge. The fourth time it bites the back of your hand and beads of blood well up. Along the rim of its shell run old marks — knife cuts, the scrape of iron levers: those before you pried too. The wall stays shut.

label.en: Pour the water into the hollow

exits.means: pours his three days' water into the hollow at the wall's foot, under a stone with the dead man's sword tied point-down on the ledge above; the gui crawls in — it is the latch — the wall rumbles open, and the sword drives into its cracked shell while it bites his arm
exits._grant: 古四 (2026-10-02): the 饭桶 spat out 踏马的符 for one of 银月's tail hairs; he never tried it, folded it into his belt fold. An exit grants one item, and 古四's two (wm-danlu keep, wm-diyilu save) already carry the 饭桶 and the 回春丹 — so the bag gets it here, the first free step before the chase. One use: its card summons the 蛫 as a 护主 against 邹青松's 四蛇合围; he slaps it on blind (作者: 「这个用完就没了，留在秘境里用。」).

story.zh:
他捡起那把剑。他爬上浅窝上头那块石檐，把剑尖朝下绑在一块斗大的石头底下；背绳一头拴着石头，一头垂下来，拴在竹筒上。他把三天的水一口不剩，全倒进了那个浅窝。银月道：「那是你三天的水。」小满道：「墙后头有风，风里有潮气。有潮气，就有水。」

水声一响，那颗脑袋出来了。壳一落进去，严丝合缝，墙里头「轰隆隆」一阵闷响。它去够窝底那只竹筒——绳子一紧，檐上的石头翻了下来，剑尖朝下，正扎进壳沿靠脖子那道裂纹里。

它没有死。那颗脑袋甩回来，一口咬住了小满的左小臂，牙进了肉，咬到了骨头。他两只脚蹬住窝沿，右手攥住剑柄，拿整个身子的分量往下压。一寸，又一寸。那张嘴越咬越紧，又一点一点地松了。

那面墙从正中裂开了一道缝，一股风从缝里涌出来，暖得像春天。小满道：「它在水里活了几百年。我却拿水骗了它。」银月半天才道：「它就是门闩。……这回，拔不出来了。」

便在这时，头顶上传来一阵脚步声。「——我就说他往这边走了！」
story.en:
He picked up the sword. He climbed onto the stone eave above the hollow and lashed the sword point-down under a rock as big as a bushel. He tied one end of the strap to the rock and let the other end hang down and tied it to his bamboo water tube. He poured three days' water into the hollow, every drop. Yinyue said: "That's your water for three days." Xiaoman said: "There's air behind the wall, and there's damp in the air. Where there's damp, there's water."

At the sound of water, the head came out. The shell settled in without a gap, and inside the wall there was a long muffled *rumble*. It stretched its neck to reach the tube. The strap went tight; the rock on the eave tipped over, sword point down, and drove straight into the crack in the shell's rim near the neck.

It didn't die. The head whipped round and clamped onto the left forearm of Xiaoman. The teeth went into the flesh, down to the bone. He braced both feet on the rim of the hollow, gripped the hilt with his right hand, and bore down with his whole body's weight. An inch, then another inch. The jaws bit tighter and tighter, and then, little by little, loosened.

The wall split down the middle, and air came pouring out of the crack into his face, warm as spring. Xiaoman said: "It lived in water for hundreds of years. And I tricked it with water." It was a long while before Yinyue said: "It was the door bolt... This time it won't come out again."

Just then came footsteps overhead. "—I told you he came this way!"

story_full.zh:
他等那颗脑袋缩稳了，才从石缝里溜下来，贴着崖根摸到塌石边，捡起那把剑。剑刃上一个缺口也没有。他爬上浅窝上头那块石檐，解下包袱的背绳，把剑尖朝下绑在一块斗大的石头底下；石头搁在檐口上，只搁了一半，背绳一头拴着石头，一头垂下来，拴在竹筒上。他溜下来，拔了竹筒塞子，把三天的水一口不剩，全倒进了那个浅窝，竹筒搁在窝底。银月道：「那是你三天的水。」小满道：「墙后头有风，风里有潮气。有潮气，就有水。」

水声一响，那颗脑袋出来了。它闻了一闻，四条腿撑起那口铁锅，一步一挪，挪进了浅窝。壳一落进去，严丝合缝，墙里头「轰隆隆」一阵闷响。它把脖子伸得老长，去够窝底那只竹筒——绳子一紧，檐上的石头翻了下来，剑尖朝下，正扎进壳沿靠脖子那道裂纹里。

它没有死。它是活了不知几百年的东西，挨了这一下，整口铁锅掀起半尺来高，那颗脑袋甩回来，一口咬住了伏在窝边的小满的左小臂，牙进了肉，咬到了骨头，一扯，把他拖倒在壳沿上。那张嘴不松，脑袋往壳里缩，要把他的胳膊一起拖进去。小满抽不出手，也没有运功。剑柄就在它脖子边上，离那张嘴不到一尺。他两只脚蹬住窝沿，右手攥住剑柄，拿整个身子的分量往下压。一寸，又一寸。那张嘴越咬越紧，又一点一点地松了。

那面墙从正中裂开了一道缝，一股风从缝里涌出来，扑在他脸上，暖得像春天。小满掰开那张嘴，把胳膊抽出来，撕下一截袄襟缠上，血一会儿就透了。他看着窝底那只翻倒的竹筒，一滴水也没剩，道：「那是三天的水。」顿了一顿，又道：「它在水里活了几百年。我却拿水骗了它。」银月半天才道：「它就是门闩。……这回，拔不出来了。」往年潭是满的，它不渴，一辈子没挪进那个窝；前人见了它，不是打，就是撬；这扇门，从来没开过。

便在这时，头顶上传来一阵脚步声，碎石子一阵一阵往下落。「——我就说他往这边走了！」
story_full.en:
He waited until the head had pulled in and settled, then slid down out of his crack, crept along the cliff foot to the rockfall, and picked up the sword. Not a notch on the blade. He climbed onto the stone eave above the hollow, took off the strap of his bundle, and lashed the sword point-down under a rock as big as a bushel. He set the rock on the lip of the eave, only half on, tied one end of the strap to the rock and let the other end hang down and tied it to his bamboo water tube. He slid down, pulled the tube's stopper, and poured three days' water into the hollow, every drop, and set the tube in the bottom of the hollow. Yinyue said: "That's your water for three days." Xiaoman said: "There's air behind the wall, and there's damp in the air. Where there's damp, there's water."

At the sound of water, the head came out. It sniffed, then pushed up that iron pot on its four legs and, a step and a shuffle at a time, shuffled into the hollow. The shell settled in without a gap, and inside the wall there was a long muffled *rumble*. It stretched its neck far out to reach the tube at the bottom of the hollow. The strap went tight; the rock on the eave tipped over, sword point down, and drove straight into the crack in the shell's rim near the neck.

It didn't die. It was a thing that had lived who knew how many hundred years. Taking that blow, the whole iron pot heaved up half a foot, and the head whipped round and clamped onto the left forearm of Xiaoman, who was crouched at the edge of the hollow. The teeth went into the flesh, down to the bone, and a jerk pulled him over onto the shell's rim. The jaws didn't let go. The head was pulling back into the shell, to drag his arm in with it. Xiaoman couldn't pull his arm free, and he didn't use any cultivation either. The sword hilt was right beside its neck, less than a foot from that mouth. He braced both feet on the rim of the hollow, gripped the hilt with his right hand, and bore down with his whole body's weight. An inch, then another inch. The jaws bit tighter and tighter, and then, little by little, loosened.

The wall split down the middle, and air came pouring out of the crack into his face, warm as spring. Xiaoman prised the jaws apart, pulled his arm out, tore a strip off the front of his jacket and bound it; the blood soaked through in moments. He looked at the overturned bamboo tube at the bottom of the hollow, not a drop left in it, and said: "That was three days' water." He paused, then said: "It lived in water for hundreds of years. And I tricked it with water." It was a long while before Yinyue said: "It was the door bolt... This time it won't come out again." In other years the pool had been full and it wasn't thirsty, and in all its life it had never moved into that hollow; the people before, when they saw it, either fought it or tried to lever it; this door had never once been opened.

Just then came footsteps overhead, and gravel trickled down in spatters. "—I told you he came this way!"

withdrawn.en: The gui draws back into the pool, then pokes its red head out again and stares at you unblinking. — Again.

refuse.en: The stone isn't on the eave yet. Set the drop first.
